C05 is another very close contemporaneous cabinet-resignation model with the same operative and encomiastic sequence. C09 is relevant because it concerns an earlier Secretary of the Interior and similarly praises administration of the Department and development of western natural resources, but its wording and structure are less close.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"I have your letter of January seventh and, in accordance with your wish, I am accepting your resignation effective at the end of my term of office.","parent_excerpt":"I have your letter and I accept your resignation as Secretary of Defense, effective at the end of the President's term of office, January 20, 1953, as you desire.","explanation":"Distinctively close opening formulation combining acknowledgment of the letter, acceptance at the official's wish, and effectiveness at the end of the presidential term."},{"child_excerpt":"I am grateful for the energy and wisdom with which you have administered the Department of Interior.","parent_excerpt":"As we both prepare to leave office, I thank you for your devotion and your wisdom and your skill.","explanation":"Both conclude their assessment with personal gratitude framed around closely overlapping qualities, including wisdom, as both officials prepare to leave office."},{"child_excerpt":"You have done an outstanding job for your Government. The conservation and wise development of our natural resources, which are entrusted to your Department, have been in good hands.","parent_excerpt":"The splendid achievements of the Department of Defense in these last years must be attributed in large part to your vision and deep understanding... You have discharged your duties well and faithfully.","explanation":"Parallel central machinery: attribute departmental achievements to the departing secretary, commend capable discharge of duties, and connect that service to a major national interest."}]}
